title: Drain-land (resident merge-queue daemon)
summary: The plateau-app resident drain daemon (tools/drain-daemon/daemon.mjs) holds the whole-process drain lease and runs scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs --label=ready-to-merge --json as a one-shot child pass on a 60s interval from a dedicated, self-syncing WE clone. All drain LOGIC (mergeability, JIT numbering, resolve-on-land, rebase-drop) stays single-sourced in WE scripts/; the daemon only schedules it. Confirmed live 2026-09-26: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.plateau.drain-daemon.plist is installed and running from /Users/nicolasgilbert/workspace/plateau-drain-daemon, driving the WE clone at .lanes/we-drain-daemon/lane-1.

provides.name: <daemon-clone>
provides.note: WorkingDirectory=/Users/nicolasgilbert/workspace/plateau-drain-daemon (the daemon's own self-syncing plateau-app checkout; confirmed live via plutil -p, 2026-09-26)

provides.name: DRAIN_DAEMON_WE_CLONE
provides.note: points at the dedicated single-lane WE pool clone the child pass actually runs in (.lanes/we-drain-daemon/lane-1) — a DIFFERENT directory than cwd:<daemon-clone> above

states.label: PR carries ready-to-merge / review:accepted
states.notes: A single-PR FAST DRAIN (scripts/pr-land.mjs, scripts/lane-drain.mjs) can also land a PR by BYPASSING the whole-process lease entirely (README.md: '/pr\`/\`/finish\` single-PR fast drains bypass the lease and stay instant') — not modeled as a separate entry here since it converges on the same merge-candidate-evaluation/merge-attempt machinery; the numbering mutex (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:5088) is what actually serializes the two paths, not this state. PR #2764 (2026-09-26, same incident as ci-heal.flow.json's ci-red transition) added a SEPARATE per-pass bookkeeping branch that runs here for EVERY PR in this sweep's context regardless of merge decision: once a PR's required check reads positively green (isRequiredCheckGreen), any CI_LIFECYCLE_OWNED label it still carries (checking/failed/blocked) is stripped via `gh pr edit --remove-label` (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:3712,3819-3829) — best-effort, a failed removal is silently retried next pass, never blocks the sweep. This clears the STALE LABEL itself (what a human/board sees); it is independent of whether ci-heal.flow.json's own ci-red→ci-heal-dispatch branch ever ran for this PR.

states.label: Whole-process drain lease: acquire, hold, or wait it out

wait.for: a foreign lease holder (an interactive session drain) to release or its 15-min TTL to expire

states.notes: Deliberately unbounded BY DESIGN ('mixed mode is permanent', plateau:tools/drain-daemon/README.md — a foreign holder is WAITED OUT, never contended). WE 4222 closed the honest gap this used to be: past the timeout the daemon still never contends, but it now fires a ONE-TIME operator notice per holder episode (decideLeaseWaitEscalation) instead of staying silent forever.

states.label: One child merge-ai-prs.mjs sweep in flight

retries.what: consecutive failed passes (exit 2 merge-attempt-failed, exit 4 child-detected failure, or a spawn/kill failure) — exponential backoff, ceiling 900s, repeats indefinitely

escalation.how: best-effort desktop notification (osascript) once anomaly detection trips on the in-memory recent-pass window — never on every single failure

states.notes: Timeout kill is SIGTERM then, after 10s, SIGKILL (plateau:tools/drain-daemon/daemon.mjs:296-300); the killed pass's unlanded PRs simply ride the next pass — no partial-merge risk since the merge itself is one atomic gh pr merge call downstream. WE 4222: the retry itself stays uncapped BY DESIGN (a drain must keep trying) — the cap only decides when to fire a one-time operator notice (decideFailureEscalation), never when to stop retrying.

states.label: REBASE_DROP: rebuild a BEHIND/conflicting-manifest PR onto main, in-pass
states.notes: CORRECTS a stale note this flow used to carry on merge-candidate-evaluation ('BEHIND ... is NOT repaired by this flow'): it IS repaired, in this SAME child pass, before classifyPr's per-PR evaluation ever sees a CONFLICTING/BEHIND verdict (or one that is landable but still carries the transient manifest, #2183). rebaseDropManifest (scripts/lib/rebase-drop-manifest.mjs) merge-trees the lane ref onto origin/main and commits+pushes a rebuilt tip; its own skip boundary (a real, non-manifest conflict) retries with the wider rebaseDropContent (scripts/lib/rebase-drop-content.mjs), which only auto-resolves when every conflicting hunk is non-overlapping (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:4120-4131). A remote-repo PR with no sibling clone provisioned is left for its author (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:4111-4114, 'skipped-remote'). #x8pcbf3 (live incident, PR #2752, fixed PR #2761, 2026-09-26): when either rebuild's own merge-tree probe fails `fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories`, that failure is FIXED AND RETRIED once — never surfaced as a real conflict on the first try — via the shared `ensureFullHistory` helper (scripts/lib/git-run.mjs:165-174, `parseIsShallow` at :135-141): probe `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository`; if shallow, `git fetch <remote> --unshallow` once and retry the SAME merge-tree once (scripts/lib/rebase-drop-manifest.mjs:149-164; scripts/lib/rebase-drop-content.mjs:317-329). A checkout that was never shallow, or one that is still shallow after a failed unshallow fetch, or one that STILL fails 'unrelated histories' after a successful unshallow, all fall through to the ordinary conflict/error handling unchanged — this is a bounded, one-shot fix, never a loop, and never a distinct new state/status of its own. The SAME shared helper also fixes this identical checkout defect in two OTHER cadences this flow file does not model at all — scripts/conveyor/branch-sync.mjs (its own merge-tree probe, branch-sync.mjs:276-296) and scripts/conveyor/branch-drift.mjs (its own drift computation, branch-drift.mjs:188-199) — genuinely out of scope here; see their own file headers, not a flow file, for how they behave.

states.label: Per-PR merge/skip decision (merge-ai-prs.mjs#classifyPr)
states.notes: decision==='merge' requires ALL of: producer-certified, required check green, mergeable==='MERGEABLE', mergeStateStatus CLEAN/UNSTABLE, non-empty body, and no uncleared review hold (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:584-615). A verdict that reaches here still BEHIND/conflicting-manifest is one rebase-drop-attempt (upstream, same pass) either skipped (real conflict beyond auto-resolution, or no sibling clone for a remote repo) or never ran (REBASE_DROP disabled) — reported here as an ordinary skip, retried next sweep unchanged.

states.label: Accepted / ready-to-merge, but ZERO check runs on this head

wait.for: something to notice this head was never actually checked and re-trigger CI or escalate

retries.what: the drain silently re-evaluates and re-skips this exact PR every ~60s sweep, forever, with no attempt count kept anywhere

states.notes: KEY QUESTION answered (the #2729 shape): reduceCheckState's empty-rollup case reads 'unchecked', never 'red' (scripts/operations/pr-status.mjs:140-147) — so merge-ai-prs.mjs's own gate reports the flat, indistinguishable-from-still-running reason 'required check "test" is not green' (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:602) every sweep, with no escalation and no comment posted. Upstream, scripts/progress-board.mjs#classifyPr's ciFailed() is `false` on an empty rollup (scripts/progress-board.mjs:466-472,510), so the SAME PR reads as board-status 'queued' — healthy-looking — meaning scripts/conveyor/reconcile-core.mjs's whole ci-red branch (ci-heal dispatch, cap-exhausted note) never even sees it either. Nobody owns this PR: not the drain (repeats the skip forever), not reconcile-core (never classifies it as needing help), not the operator queue (no distinguishing signal to surface). The most common real cause is exactly ci-heal.flow.json's base-retargeted state (a stacked PR's base merges, GitHub retargets it onto main with no fresh CI run) — but this state is reached whenever a head genuinely has zero check runs for ANY reason, not only that one.

states.label: fix-couple-split: hold either half of a cross-repo couple whose partner isn't landing this pass

retries.what: a held couple member (impl half or WE carrier) is re-evaluated fresh next sweep with no attempt count kept — if its partner never lands (e.g. the partner PR is closed/abandoned), nothing distinguishes that from a partner merely landing on a LATER pass

states.notes: PR #2763 (fix-couple-split, 2026-09-26): a cross-repo couple (a frontierui/plateau-app impl half + its WE carrier) lands WHOLE in one pass or not at all. Two mechanisms: (1) HOLD — every couple member whose partner is not landing this pass is held (fixpoint over held partners), contiguous ORDER — impl half(s) then the carrier immediately — so no other merge can move `main` between the two halves (scripts/lib/couple-cascade.mjs#planCoupleCascadeStep); (2) a carrier PREFLIGHT — right before an impl half merges, the carrier's FRESH re-read must still say 'merge', else BOTH halves are held (scripts/lib/couple-cascade.mjs#carrierPreflight, scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:4890-4907). Live incident this closes: pass 2026-09-26T20:32:20Z merged plateau-app#185 (impl), then web-everything#2746 (unrelated) moved WE main, then #2751 (#185's carrier) re-read BEHIND and was refused — the impl had already landed alone. The couple-gate's own hold-forever exposure (no cap on how many passes the SAME couple can be held if its partner genuinely never lands) is the SAME class of gap #2989 already tracks for the upstream couple-JOIN mechanism (joinImplToCouples, which decides which impl is attached to which carrier BEFORE this gate ever sees it) — adjacent, not identical, but acknowledged there rather than re-filed. RESIDUAL this gate cannot close: the carrier's own `gh pr merge` can still fail AFTER its impl half already landed (a GitHub error in the ~1s between the two writes — two repos cannot merge atomically); reported as `coupleSplit` (JSON + a loud stderr line, scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:4924-4926,4978,5152) but nothing beyond that log line pages an operator, retries with priority, or caps how many times the SAME split can recur silently-except-for-a-log-line — tracked as its own gap, card 4247.

states.label: gh pr merge via the shared merge gate

retries.what: a failed real merge attempt (a genuine race: the head moved between the pass's own re-confirmation and this call, guarded by --match-head-commit) is retried next sweep with no count kept

states.notes: A merge failure on a PR the SAME pass just rebase-dropped is expected (CI is re-running against the new tip) and is not treated as a fault (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:4988-4993); every other merge failure is reported in failedMerges and simply retried the next sweep.

states.label: JIT numbering + resolve-on-land + primary/local ff-sync
states.notes: withNumberingLock is a TTL-bounded mutex (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:5088); on contention it proceeds WITHOUT the lock rather than waiting (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:5178, 'numbered without it ... the #2318 duplicate-NNN tripwire is the backstop') — the tripwire is the ONLY thing that catches a real collision, and only on a LATER pass. resolve-on-land totality (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:5143-5164) reports every landed item into exactly one of resolved/already-resolved/deferred/failed, so a withheld flip is at least visible in the pass's own stderr/--json — never a fully silent drop.

states.label: Cross-repo couple split: impl half landed, its WE carrier's merge then failed
states.notes: The couple-gate's own residual it cannot close (see couple-gate's notes): reached only when a carrier PASSED carrierPreflight (or already had merged impls) and its OWN `gh pr merge` still failed right after — a real, rare race (two repos, one write each, ~1s apart). Reported into the pass's JSON `coupleSplit` array plus one loud stderr line (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:4924-4926) — that IS the whole escalation today; nothing pages an operator, nothing retries this specific carrier with priority, and nothing caps how many passes the SAME split can recur, each producing only another log line. The carrier itself still rejoins the ordinary merge-attempt retry loop next sweep (this state is an ADDITIONAL classification layered on that failure, not a replacement terminus) — tracked as its own gap, card 4247.

states.label: Merged, numbered, resolved, leases released
states.notes: The drain's terminal land event is the universal owner of post-land cleanup for every land path (scripts/lane-drain.mjs:33-40) — resolveLandedItem (scripts/lane-drain.mjs:1059) flips active/open→resolved, releaseItemLeases (scripts/lane-drain.mjs:1090, called at :481) releases every held lease.

states.label: Duplicate NNN survives on main — globally red

escalation.how: a loud daemon.log line naming the incident + a best-effort desktop notification (osascript); polling cannot clear it

retries.what: the daemon still re-attempts the sweep every 900s (the backoff ceiling) forever — the escalation never actually stops the retrying, it only makes it loud

states.notes: Detected only on exit 3 WITHOUT a carried reason (a bare process.exit(3) after the full report, never a fail('gh-error',...) call) — an exit 3 that DOES carry reason:'gh-error' (a transient gh error) takes the ordinary generic backoff instead and is never treated as this incident (plateau:tools/drain-daemon/lib.mjs:421-434). 'Polling cannot clear it' per the daemon's own README — this is explicitly an operator-only fix (WE #2318). WE 4222: a duplicate-NNN failure folds into the SAME consecutiveFailures counter as any other failed pass (decideFailureEscalation makes no special case for it), so the SAME 6-failure cap and the SAME shared failure-streak-escalated notice cover this incident too.

states.label: Foreign lease wait exceeded the alert bound — operator notified once for this holder

escalation.how: daemon.log line + desktop notification + state-file leaseWaitEscalated, once per holder

states.notes: The daemon still never contends — it keeps waiting out the SAME holder exactly as lease-arbitration always did (WE 4222 only adds the notice, decideLeaseWaitEscalation). Loops back to lease-arbitration: the next tick re-arbitrates (still waiting, or the holder released/expired and this daemon acquires).

states.label: Consecutive failed passes reached the cap — operator notified once for this streak

escalation.how: daemon.log line + desktop notification + state-file failureStreakEscalated, once per streak

states.notes: Reached from pass-running's ordinary exponential-backoff failures AND from duplicate-nnn-parked's exit-3 park — decideFailureEscalation folds both into the SAME consecutiveFailures counter (WE 4222), so one cap covers both causes. Loops back to pass-running: the drain keeps retrying at the same backoff ceiling (a drain must keep trying — the cap's exit is 'a person is told', not 'stop').

transitions.on: the next 60s tick
lease held by a foreign owner — wait it out
lease acquired (or already held by this daemon)
child pass reads the candidate set; a verdict is CONFLICTING/BEHIND, or landable but still carrying the transient manifest (#2183), and REBASE_DROP is enabled
child pass reads the ready-to-merge/review:accepted candidate set; verdicts not eligible for rebase-drop go straight to evaluation
rebased onto main, or already current/manifest-free — decision flipped to 'merge', proceeds into this SAME pass's ordinary evaluation
skip: a real conflict beyond the content resolver's safe (non-overlapping) hunks, or a remote repo with no sibling clone provisioned — left for the PR's author, retried next sweep
decision === 'merge' — every ready candidate passes through the couple-atomicity gate; a plain (non-couple) PR is never held there
not a couple member, or a couple member whose partner clears (already merged this pass, or lands right after it in the same contiguous group)
held: partner half not landing this pass (or its own carrier preflight failed) — decision downgraded to skip, re-evaluated fresh next sweep
required check has zero runs on this head (reduceCheckState:'unchecked') despite review:accepted/ready-to-merge
mergeStateStatus === 'DIRTY' — a real conflict with main
any other skip (not certified, non-default base, required check red/pending, BEHIND, empty body, uncleared review hold) — retried next sweep
next sweep, unchanged
gh pr merge succeeded
merge failed (race lost, or a real fault) — retried next sweep
the failing PR is a WE carrier whose impl half(s) already merged THIS pass — an ADDITIONAL classification alongside the ordinary failure above, never a replacement for it
numbering + resolve-on-land + ff-sync all completed (best-effort, non-fatal throughout)
a later pass discovers two files claiming the same NNN survives on main
the lease was reclaimed away mid-pass (heartbeat failed — slept past the TTL, or a foreign holder took over); the in-flight child is killed
the wait on the SAME foreign holder exceeds the 30m alert bound (decideLeaseWaitEscalation), not yet notified for this holder episode
next tick — still waiting it out (never contending), or the lease is now free/stale to acquire
consecutiveFailures reaches the 6-failure cap after a failed pass, not yet escalated for this streak (decideFailureEscalation)
the SAME consecutiveFailures counter (a duplicate-NNN park counts as a failure) reaches the 6-failure cap, not yet escalated for this streak
next tick — the drain retries at the same backoff ceiling regardless (a drain must keep trying)

steps.does: dl.acquireDrainLease(DRAIN_LOCK_ROOT, OWNER, {repoKey}) once the lease reads free/stale
steps.notes: A lost race (another process acquired first) simply loops back to re-arbitrate next tick — never a dead end.

steps.does: git fetch + reset --hard origin/main + clean -fdq on the dedicated WE clone; npm ci --ignore-scripts only when the lockfile changed
steps.notes: canFail with no dedicated onFailure state: a refresh failure just logs a WARN and the pass runs on the existing (possibly stale) checkout (plateau:tools/drain-daemon/daemon.mjs:277-280) — never blocks or reroutes, so onFailure loops back into the same pass-running state the next step (spawn-child-pass) already runs in.

steps.does: spawns `node scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs --label=ready-to-merge --json --under-lease=<OWNER>` with cwd=the WE clone

provides.name: <we-drain-clone>
provides.note: the CHILD's own cwd, inherited from spawn()'s cwd option

steps.does: certified? required-check green? mergeable? landable mergeStateStatus? non-empty body? review hold cleared?
steps.notes: This assumption is never actually confirmed here (or anywhere else in this flow) — GitHub's rollup is trusted as-is whatever produced it. accepted-unchecked-no-ci is what happens when the assumption is false (zero runs at all); ci-heal.flow.json's base-retargeted state names the most common concrete cause.

steps.does: gh pr merge <n> --<method> --delete-branch --match-head-commit <sha> — the ONE place a gh pr merge to main may originate

provides.name: mergeable
provides.note: re-confirmed by classifyPr's own fresh re-read immediately before this call (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:619-629)

steps.does: assigns the real sequential NNN to every hash-keyed item now on main, then flips active/open→resolved for every fully-landed couple, then pushes both in one commit
steps.notes: Best-effort/non-fatal throughout, matching the numbering critical section's own posture — a push failure surfaces a warning (scripts/merge-ai-prs.mjs:5172-5174) but never unwinds the already-green land, so onFailure lands on the same pr-landed terminus the success path reaches (the PR itself is already merged before this housekeeping runs).
